% Beamer source: an itemize with a $$...$$ display in the middle of it. The
% spelling is harmless here -- Beamer indents all three items identically, and so
% does article. Under ltx-talk 0.5.3 every \item AFTER the display loses the list
% indentation and renders flush with the frame margin, so the list visibly splits
% in two (C-DISPLAY-DOLLAR).
%
% Measured with pdftotext -bbox, x-position of the item text in points:
%   $$...$$  ->  50.0 / 28.3 / 28.3     (items 2 and 3 lose the 21.7pt indent)
%   \[...\]  ->  50.0 / 50.0 / 50.0
% Nothing warns: clean compile, right page count, sound tag tree, and pdftotext
% returns the same words in the same order. Only a rendered page shows it.
%
% One real 20-lecture course had this in 16 of 24 decks across 164 sites, found
% by eye months after conversion.
\documentclass{beamer}

\begin{document}
\begin{frame}
\frametitle{Utilities}
\begin{itemize}
\item A utility function maps states to reals
$$U:S \to R$$
\item The agent maximises expected utility
\item Preferences must be transitive
\end{itemize}
\end{frame}
\end{document}
